newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Ashland targets sharp European sales growth.
newsitem.headline: Ashland targets sharp European sales growth.

text.p: U.S. energy and chemicals firm Ashland Inc said on Wednesday its turnover in Europe should top $1 billion by 2000 and a new European administrative headquarters in the Netherlands would pare costs.
"We expect (sales of) around $700 million this year and our aim is to break through $1 billion by the year 2000," Chairman and Chief Executive Officer Paul Chellgren told Reuters.

Chellgren was speaking at a news conference to mark the opening of Ashland's new "Shared Services Centre" in Rotterdam, a European "back office" Ashland believes is vital if it is to boost its presence on the continent.
"It is an essential part of our strategy, inevitably cutting costs... and providing services to around 75 separate units (in Europe)," Chellgren said.

Motor oils and chemicals have been the fastest growing and most profitable parts of Ashland's business and Chellgren believes both will continue to grow, with Europe identified as a key battle ground.
He said Ashland has a sure foothold across western Europe from which it could become a leading player selling speciality chemicals, and motor oils in growing east European markets.
He added this expansion was likely to result more through acquisitions than organic growth.
Within the Ashland group, motor oils unit Valvoline has set itself a target of doubling turnover in Europe in five years.
The emphasis on chemicals and motor oils partly results from a recognition of the margin squeeze in oil refining.

Chellgren said he saw little growth in Ashland's oil business, although cost savings would result from the recently announced joint venture with USX Corp's Marathon in which Ashland will take a 38 percent stake.
Chellgren said they did not yet know how large these savings would be.
Ashland Inc's 1996 turnover was $13.1 billion, of which $3.7 billion came from chemicals and $1.2 billion from Valvoline.
